ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
In a uniform electric field, points A and B lie on the same electric field line. The electric field strength is given as $E = 2.0 \times 10^{4} \mathrm{N/C}$, and the distance between points A and B is $d = 0.20 \mathrm{m}$. A test charge with charge $q = +1.0 \times 10^{-8} \mathrm{C}$ is moved from point A to point B.

1. The magnitude of the electrostatic force $F$ experienced by the test charge in the electric field.
2. In this process, the work done by the electrostatic force on the test charge is $W$.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: In a uniform electric field, points A and B lie on the same electric field line. The electric field strength is given as $E = 2.0 \times 10^{4} \, \mathrm{N/C}$, and the distance between points A and B is $d = 0.20 \, \mathrm{m}$. A test charge with charge $q = +1.0 \times 10^{-8} \, \mathrm{C}$ is moved from point A to point B. 1. ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are multiple horizontal electric field lines parallel to one another, and the arrows all point to the right; E is marked on the right side. Point A and point B are located on the same horizontal electric field line, and A is on the left and B is on the right, so the direction of displacement from A to B is to the right, the same as the direction of the electric field. Reasoning calculation: It is known that the electric field strength E = 2.0×10^4 N/C, and the test charge q = +1.0×10^-8 C. The magnitude of the electric field force is obtained from F = qE: F = (1.0×10^-8 C)(2.0×10^4 N/C) = 2.0×10^-4 N. Since the charge is positive, the direction of the electric field force is the same as the direction of the electric field; the displacement from A to B in the figure is also along the direction of the electric field, so the angle between the force and the displacement is 0°. The work W = Fd cos 0° = qEd = (2.0×10^-4 N)(0.20 m) = 4.0×10^-5 J.
